The deal could materialize in coming weeks, but no agreement has been confirmed. Modine's data center business has boomed with 95% sales growth last quarter, and the company recently spun off its automotive business to focus on cooling solutions. The company's BASX brand saw sales surge 218% to $397.2 million. Management raised full-year sales growth guidance to 72%-75% and expanded its credit facility to $1.2 billion. LUNR.headline: LUNR Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Growth and 2027 Outlook
LUNR.description: Intuitive Machines (LUNR) reported Q3 revenues of $269.3M, beating estimates, with adjusted EBITDA turning positive at $8.3M. The company refined its 2026 revenue guidance to $920-950M and highlighted a record $1.9B backlog. Management expects 40-45% of the backlog to convert to 2027 revenues as lunar deployment accelerates, with the IM-3 mission targeted for March-April 2027.

LUNR.headline: Can LUNR Convert Its Record Backlog Into Sustained Growth?
LUNR.description: Intuitive Machines (LUNR) reported record Q3 2026 revenues of $269 million with a contracted backlog reaching $1.9 billion, driven by new awards including NASA's CLPS 2 program and defense contracts. The company projects 2026 revenues of $920-$950 million with positive adjusted EBITDA, though execution risks remain. LUNR trades at a premium valuation (2.65X P/S) and holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

LUNR.headline: Intuitive Machines, Inc. (LUNR) Reports Q3 Loss, Beats Revenue Estimates
LUNR.description: Intuitive Machines (LUNR) reported a Q3 loss of $0.10 per share, beating the consensus estimate of $0.12 loss, with a 16.67% earnings surprise. Revenue of $269.35 million surpassed estimates by 10.70%, up significantly from $52.44 million year-ago. However, the stock has underperformed the market, down 25% year-to-date versus the S&P 500's 11.3% gain. The company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with mixed estimate revisions.

AMD.headline: AMD or Intel: 1 Chip Stock Is the Clear Winner
AMD.description: AMD emerges as the superior investment choice compared to Intel, demonstrating stronger financial results with 45% revenue growth versus Intel's 21%, higher gross margins (54% vs 40%), and faster data center segment growth (97% vs 78%). AMD's better execution in outsourced manufacturing, stronger positioning for agentic AI demand, and more reasonable valuation (30.7x forward earnings vs Intel's 34.4x) make it the clear winner.

AMD.headline: Why Advanced Micro Devices Stock Is Down Today
AMD.description: AMD stock fell 10.8% on November 13, 2026, as the chip sector sold off following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation due to a scandal involving an alleged affair with a Chinese spy who helped divert $7.5 billion in Nvidia chips to China. While AMD initially gained on hopes of capturing diverted orders, investors grew concerned about broader industry risks and potential regulatory fallout. AMD.headline: Why Micron Stock Was Sliding Today
AMD.description: Micron stock fell 5.25% as part of a broader semiconductor sector sell-off following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO. The uncertainty surrounding Nvidia's leadership and the future of the AI boom has created investor malaise across the chip sector. Since Micron's surge has been driven by AI-related memory chip demand and Nvidia is its biggest customer, the company is particularly sensitive to sentiment shifts in the AI industry.

AMD.headline: NVIDIA Leadership Crisis Opens Door for Chip Rivals? ETFs in Focus
AMD.description: Following Jensen Huang's resignation as NVIDIA CEO due to personal scandals, investors are rotating toward competing semiconductor companies including AMD, Broadcom, and TSMC. While NVIDIA shares fell 4.3%, AMD and Broadcom gained 5.9% and 5.5% respectively. Despite the management uncertainty, the broader AI investment cycle remains strong, though growing competition could eventually commoditize AI capabilities and pressure chip prices.

AMD.headline: Anthropic Delivers Huge News for Nvidia Stock, AMD Stock, Micron Stock, and Broadcom Stock Investors
AMD.description: Anthropic's potential IPO could be a significant event for AI stock investors, particularly benefiting semiconductor and chip companies like Nvidia, AMD, Micron, and Broadcom that supply AI infrastructure and components.

AMD.headline: Will the US Blue Wave Wash Out Semiconductors? Judging Through the ETF Lens
AMD.description: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged over 12% following Democratic control of Congress, as investors feared regulatory pressure on AI data-center expansion. However, strong structural demand persists with DRAM prices up 484% year-over-year and major chipmakers securing long-term contracts with hyperscalers. Despite short-term political headwinds, semiconductor fundamentals remain intact, presenting potential buying opportunities through diversified ETF exposure.

AMD.headline: The AI Trade Just Cracked. Here’s the Price at Which I’d Start Buying Nvidia.
AMD.description: Nvidia stock plummeted following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid personal scandals. The stock fell below $150 from a record high of $243 in October 2026. Despite current turmoil and succession risks, the analyst sees the sell-off as a buying opportunity at $155-160 per share, citing an attractive forward P/E ratio of 9.7-10.1x based on fiscal 2028 earnings estimates. The broader AI sector faces headwinds as investors question hyperscaler returns on AI infrastructure investments.

AMD.headline: Is Nvidia Undervalued?
AMD.description: Nvidia stock has plummeted 30% from its all-time high following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation due to personal conduct issues. Despite the turmoil, the company's financial performance remains strong with 106% revenue growth and 120% earnings growth in Q2 FY2027. AMD.headline: Stock Market Today, Nov. 12: AMD Jumps 5.9% on Bank of America Price Target Hike to $700
AMD.description: AMD surged 5.9% to $585.30 after Bank of America raised its price target to $700, citing strong chip demand. The rally was also fueled by investor rotation into semiconductor peers following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and William Blair's upgrade of AMD. AMD's data center segment showed 97% yearly revenue growth, with expectations for server revenue to double in 2027. However, AMD's valuation remains elevated with a P/E ratio of 127.

AMD.headline: Prediction: $500 a Month Invested in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Will Be Worth This Much by 2030
AMD.description: The article analyzes potential returns from monthly $500 investments in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) through 2030. Based on three scenarios with 10%, 12.5%, and 25% annual returns, investments could grow to $23,958, $25,629, and $35,156 respectively.
